defects.detail: MOVE middle phases show a long gray rectangular side strip extending down alongside the body; separate wing articulation is difficult to read as a flap. Head/body remain coherent, so this is an appendage-readability limitation rather than a proven joint break.

MOVE changes the thin sprawling limbs of Idle/Play into broad hanging columns/merged masses, obscuring torso/limb boundaries and readable articulation. Head/spot pattern remains associated; this is visible pose distortion, not a claim of numerical joint failure.

The MOVE row develops a thick slab-like left/lower appendage and merged central limb mass compared with thin sprawling Idle limbs; the pose reads as soft stretching rather than clear crawling articulation.

Even the first pictured MOVE phase has broad down-hanging limb columns, unlike the thin sprawling Idle limbs. Subsequent phases preserve that bulky merged appearance, limiting limb/body separation and crawling readability.

limitations: This receipt records an agent's direct inspection of the listed 40 PNG sheets. No human review is claimed.

Each sheet contains four action rows and eight pictured phases, at developmental day 75. These 1,280 pictured frames are separate from primary lifecycle coverage and the automated supplemental motion checks.
The eight static samples cover 0 to 1.75 seconds in 0.25-second steps. They do not establish continuous smoothness, every transition, or complete animation cycles.
Idle and settled Play are often near-static at this sheet scale. The short sample window does not establish whether a full blink cycle works or fails.
The configured target is not drawn on the sheets. Catch/contact status and contact geometry cannot be visually confirmed from these target-free images.
Jagged edges, fine appendages and overlapping paint can be ambiguous. A visible readability problem is not proof of a numerical joint failure or source-organ loss.
Movement is pictured in place without terrain, world travel or physics context.
